text.p: Headlines from major national newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
EL PAIS
- Disagreement among EU leaders delays Maastricht reforms
- (Interior Minister) Mayor Oreja said four or five ETA prisoners to be transferred nearer the Basque country.
- Telefonica fined 110 million pesetas for giving private information about its clients.
- Spanish Digital TV Canal Satellite, in which Sogecable has a 85 percent stake, to increase its capital up to 26 billion pesetas.
EL MUNDO
- 59 percent of PSOE voters want Guerra to stay as deputy secretary.
- The government will increase expenditure by 350 billion pesetas to reform health system in 1998.
- The fight for power in the European Union paralysed its enlargement toward the East.
ABC
- Amsterdam summit ends without crucial agreement, though Spain saved its vital interests
CINCO DIAS
- Are stocks too expensive? Only British shares considered cheaper than Spanish.
- Codorniu launched a friendly bid for 100 percent of winery Bodega Bilbaina.
- Savings banks take risks with Bourse investments
- Cofir bought from Grupo Catalan the 34 percent stake it did not already have of NH hotel
- Sogecable had 1996 net profit of 5.8 billion pesetas
EXPANSION
- "The 15" failed in their intention to reform the European Union.
- Spanish government to increase health expenditure via 1998 budget and with an improved better fraud control.
- Antonio Catalan left NH Hotel and sold 34 percent to Cofir
- Cordoniu launchs a bid for Bodegas Bilbaina
GACETA DE LOS NEGOCIOS
- Abello and Ballve to launch a 40 billion offer for Santana Motor
- Mortgage rates fell below seven percent in May
- Spanish Sevillana de Electricidad appointed Manuel Otero Luna as chairman
- Public health system will receive 120 billion more in three years.
- Airline Air Europe seen to announce few days of strike during the key days in the summer.
